items.title: Friends visual hierarchy and theme parity
items.precondition: Signed in; isolated runtime is running; open /friends.
steps: Inspect the Friends panel in the current light theme.
Hover the main Friends dashboard card and compare it with its resting state.
Verify the Friends content wrapper is absent and the section title aligns to the navigation’s left edge.
Inspect individual friend rows at rest, on hover, and when keyboard focused.
Toggle the existing dark theme and inspect again.
Open a non-Friends route such as Feed or Messages.
items.expected: The route presents a calmer Friends surface without a purple accent, content wrapper, dashboard shadow, or individual friend-row card surface; the section title aligns to the navigation and keyboard focus remains visible; other routes keep their existing card styling.

items.title: Friends, Requests, and Suggested navigation is accessible
items.precondition: Signed in; at least one mutual friend and one incoming or outgoing request available when possible.
steps: Select each navigation view with pointer input.
Use Tab and arrow keys to select views.
Repeat at 375px width.
items.expected: Each view shows the intended real data with its inline count, focus remains visible, no server write occurs when switching views, and the layout has no horizontal overflow.

items.title: Existing friend request lifecycle remains intact
items.precondition: Synthetic accounts: requester, recipient, and an unrelated user.
steps: Click Search people, enter a username in the revealed field, and submit the request.
Verify it appears in Sent Requests and disappears from Suggested if previously listed.
As the recipient, confirm and then verify it moves to Friends.
Create another request and decline or cancel it.
items.expected: Send, confirm, decline, and cancel retain current behavior; all affected panels refresh without stale rows.

items.title: Friends-of-friends suggestions are accurate and private
items.precondition: Synthetic graph: viewer is friends with Alex; Alex is friends with Bea and Casey; viewer has a pending relationship with Casey.
steps: Call GET /api/friends/suggestions as the viewer.
Inspect every returned object.
Compare the response to the graph after adding a second shared friend for Bea.
items.expected: Bea appears once with the correct mutual-friend count and outranks lower-count candidates. Viewer, Alex, Casey, and all direct/pending relationships are absent. Objects have no email field.

items.title: Suggestion endpoint is protected and index migration applies
items.precondition: Isolated acceptance database and API runtime.
steps: Run the friend-suggestion migration.
Request GET /api/friends/suggestions without authentication.
Request it with a valid authenticated session.
Inspect the database indexes or migration output.
items.expected: Migration succeeds; unauthenticated request is rejected; authenticated request succeeds; both accepted-status relationship lookup indexes are present.

items.title: Presence and friend actions are truthful and usable
items.precondition: Two mutual accounts; one connected to Socket.IO and one disconnected.
steps: Open Friends as the viewer.
Connect and disconnect the other mutual account.
Observe the row’s presence treatment.
Click Message, then open overflow and cancel Unfriend; repeat and confirm Unfriend.
items.expected: Only real mutual presence changes are shown. Message opens the existing conversation; overflow action is labeled and Unfriend still requires confirmation.

items.title: Static validation and build gate
items.precondition: Implementation complete in the linked branch worktree.
steps: Run npm run typecheck.
Run npm run build.
Run npm --prefix frontend run lint.
Run the convention check if available.
items.expected: All execution-caused type, build, lint, and convention failures are fixed before finalization.
items.evidence: 2026-08-15: npm run typecheck; npm run build; npm --prefix frontend run lint (existing unrelated warnings only).
items.notes: No automated test runner is configured in the current repository; this is not a waiver for API and isolated-runtime acceptance checks.
